title: Transfer a probationary interstate driver licence
summary: Learn how to transfer your probationary interstate driver licence to a NSW licence.
intro:
If you move to NSW from another Australian state or territory, you can only drive on an interstate licence for the first 3 months. After that period, you'll need to visit a Service NSW Centre and apply for a NSW driver licence.

Your probationary licence will be transferred to a licence of the same class with a mandatory good behaviour period provision.
who_can_apply: You must move to NSW from another Australian state or territory.
what_you_need: Evidence of the first issue date of your interstate licence
Your contact lenses or glasses (if you wear them)
Completed PDF forms: Licence Application – PDF

how_to_steps.text: Make sure you have all your documentation and any additional items (if applicable).
Visit a service centre and submit your application.

more_info.text: Renewal notices are posted generally within 6 weeks of the card's expiry date giving you plenty of time to plan ahead and renew early.
For driver licence renewals or applications, a receipt is provided that allows you to drive until the card arrives in the post. The receipt is valid for 2 months.

faqs.q: How long can I drive on my interstate licence after moving to NSW?
faqs.a: You can only drive on an interstate licence for the first 3 months after moving to NSW. After this period, you must apply for a NSW driver licence.

faqs.q: What happens when I transfer my probationary licence?
faqs.a: Your probationary licence will be transferred to a licence of the same class, which will include a mandatory good behaviour period provision.
